title: Introduction

content.content:
The tech landscape accelerates daily, yet for most CS and IT students, the path to entry level job remains dangerously unclear. Beginners often drift through a 'fog' of disconnected tutorials and generic advice, resulting in wasted time, scattered skill sets, and weak portfolios.
In the Saudi and Arab context, where digital employability is a national priority, this lack of structure is a critical gap. Mallah replaces confusion with precision. It starts by assigning a Suitable Career path based on the learner's specific goals. From there, it guides them from theory to practice—building tangible skills through real-world projects—and finally bridges the gap to employment.

content.content:
Technology beginners (CS/IT students, fresh graduates, career shifters) commonly face:
Track confusion: difficulty choosing a suitable tech path and starting point.
Unstructured learning: scattered tutorials with no sequencing, milestones, or progress visibility.
Weak outcomes: completing courses without producing real, shareable evidence. No skills record, no project portfolio, nothing a recruiter can actually see.
Job description barrier: job postings feel like a foreign language. Beginners can't map what employers ask for to what they should learn next..
Readiness uncertainty: there is no clear moment where a beginner knows they are ready to apply. Without a measurable signal, most either apply too early or keep learning indefinitely without taking action.
Core gap: learning, portfolio evidence, resume preparation, job alignment, and application tracking are rarely connected in one workflow.

Primary objective: enable beginners to move from confusion to job readiness through a guided, low-complexity workflow.
Mallah aims to provide:
Guided onboarding: AI-powered wizard that builds a complete learner profile and recommends the most suitable career path based on background, goals, weekly availability, and confidence.
Predefined roadmaps: assign users to a structured roadmap organized as Path → Stage → Topic.
Skills & Projects Hub: a verified record of earned skills and completed projects, with a public shareable profile and granular visibility control over what recruiters can see.
Smart Resume Builder: build a complete, ATS-optimized resume section by section. AI refines wording and tailors the entire resume to a specific job description on demand.
Opportunity Analyzer: paste a job description or browse the Saudi job feed to receive a match score, matched and missing skills, an AI action plan, and direct links to roadmap topics that close the gap.Application Tracker: manage the full job search pipeline from saved to offer, with one-click import from saved analyses and a direct bridge back to the original AI report for every application.

title: Methodology

content.content:
Methodology: Approach & Phases
Mallah was developed following an Agile methodology an iterative, incremental approach that allowed the team to continuously evaluate, refine, and adapt across all phases of the project lifecycle.
Planning:  defined project scope, objectives, target users, and feasibility within the Saudi digital employability context 
Requirements Analysis:  gathered requirements through literature review, competitive analysis of 7 platforms, and user needs analysis 
System Design: translated requirements into standard UML artifacts before any implementation began 
Implementation: built all 8 learner-facing features and the admin panel 
Testing & Integration: manual testing, integration testing, and feature validation across all modules 
Deployment & Maintenance: platform deployed and live, iterative improvements ongoing.

title: Methodology Cont.

content.content:
Methodology: Technical Decisions & Design Principles
The tech stack was chosen to match the system's specific requirements not convention.
The platform is built on Next.js with Feature-Sliced Design, ensuring each feature is fully self-contained and independently maintainable. Supabase (PostgreSQL) handles all data with row-level security enforced per user role. Zod validates every input at the server action layer. gpt-4o powers all AI features.
Two principles guided every decision.
AI by exception: rule-based logic was used wherever consistency and transparency were achievable. AI was reserved only for tasks that genuinely required language understanding: JD extraction, CV parsing, tutoring, and resume refinement.
Evidence over fabrication: every AI feature operates strictly on the learner's real data. The resume builder never invented experience. The analyzer only compares against verified skills. This was a deliberate product and ethical decision.

title: Conclusion

content.content:
Mallah is a web-based platform that bridges learning and employment preparation for CS/IT students, fresh graduates, and career switchers.
It guides learners through predefined roadmaps and project-based learning to produce real skills and portfolio evidence.
It then supports resume building from the learner’s actual work and analyzes job descriptions to show match level, missing skills, and next learning steps.
Overall, Mallah reduces confusion and helps learners progress toward entry-level roles with clearer, evidence-based decisions.
